breadcrumb: Std 6 Social Science Term-II (English) — Geography Unit 1: Resources — Boxed notes (தெரிந்து தெளிவோம் / Do you know)

questions.quote: Kural 736: A land that is free from any damage and, even if it is damaged, can restore it and remains sustainable, is the best country.

en.q: 'கேடறியாக் கேட்ட இடத்தும் வளங்குன்றா நாடென்ப நாட்டின் தலை' - this Kural (736) praises a country whose resources are ______.
options: largest in area among all nations
owned and ruled by one king alone
resources never decline even in troubles
rich in goods imported from abroad

ta.q: 'கேடறியாக் கேட்ட இடத்தும் வளங்குன்றா நாடென்ப நாட்டின் தலை' (குறள் 736) கூறும் சிறந்த நாடு ______.
ta.explanation: நிலையான (குன்றா) வளங்களைக் கொண்ட நாட்டைக் குறள் சிறப்பிக்கிறது.

questions.quote: Silicon, extracted from sand, a natural resource, is used in making PV cells. It converts solar energy into electrical energy. All things useful to man is resource. And if it is directly from nature we call it natural resource.

en.q: PV (photovoltaic) cells of solar panels are made from ______ extracted from sand.
en.explanation: PV cells convert solar energy into electrical energy.

ta.q: சூரிய மின்தகடுகளின் PV செல்கள் மணலிலிருந்து பெறப்படும் ______ ஆல் செய்யப்படுகின்றன.
ta.explanation: PV செல்கள் சூரிய ஆற்றலை மின்னாற்றலாக மாற்றுகின்றன.

questions.quote: Resource is anything that fulfills human needs. Commercial resources have great economic value (e.g.) Petroleum. Non-commercial resources are very abundant in availability (e.g.) Air.

en.q: Which of the following is a non-commercial resource according to the lesson?
en.explanation: Petroleum has great economic value (commercial); air is abundant and non-commercial.

ta.explanation: பெட்ரோலியம் வணிக வளம்; காற்று மிகுதியாக உள்ள வணிகமற்ற வளம்.

questions.quote: On the basis of origin, resources can be classified into biotic and abiotic resources. All living resources are biotic resources - plants, animals and other micro organisms.

en.q: On the basis of origin, natural resources are classified into ______ and abiotic resources.
en.explanation: Plants, animals and micro-organisms are biotic; land, water, air and minerals are abiotic.

ta.q: தோற்றத்தின் அடிப்படையில் இயற்கை வளங்கள் ______ மற்றும் உயிரற்ற வளங்கள் எனப் பிரிக்கப்படுகின்றன.

questions.quote: In the beginning, man had only three basic needs - food, clothing and shelter. He collected things through primary activities such as hunting, food gathering, fishing and forestry.

en.q: Which of the following is NOT a primary activity mentioned in the lesson?

ta.q: பாடத்தில் குறிப்பிடப்படும் முதல் நிலை செயல்பாடு அல்லாதது எது?

questions.quote: Resources once consumed can be renewed with the passage of time are called renewable resources. (e.g.) Air, Water, Sunlight. The resources which cannot be immediately renewed once they are depleted are called non-renewable resources.

en.q: Resources: Which of the following is a non-renewable resource?
en.explanation: Coal, petroleum, natural gas and other minerals are non-renewable; they take a long time to form.

ta.explanation: நிலக்கரி, பெட்ரோலியம், இயற்கை வாயு, கனிமங்கள் புதுப்பிக்க இயலாதவை.

questions.quote: Individual resources are resources privately owned by individuals (e.g.) Farmland. Community-owned resources can be utilised by all the members of the community (e.g.) Public parks. National resources are resources within the political boundaries and oceanic area of a country.

en.q: A public park is an example of a ______ resource.

questions.quote: Tropical rain forests are called the 'World's largest Pharmacy' as 25% of the natural vegetation are medicinal plants. (e.g.) Cinchona.

en.q: Tropical rain forests are called the 'World's largest Pharmacy' because about ______ of their natural vegetation are medicinal plants.

ta.q: வெப்ப மண்டல மழைக்காடுகள் 'உலகின் பெரும் மருந்தகம்' எனப்படக் காரணம், அங்குள்ள தாவரங்களில் ஏறத்தாழ ______ மருத்துவத் தாவரங்கள்.

questions.quote: International resources are all oceanic resources found in the open ocean. Resources found in this region can be utilized only after an international agreement. (e.g.) Ambergris. Ambergris is an extract from the sperm whale.

en.q: Ambergris, an international resource, is an extract from the ______.
en.explanation: It is used in perfume industries.

ta.q: பன்னாட்டு வளமான திமிங்கலப் புனுகு (ambergris) ______ இடமிருந்து பெறப்படுகிறது.

questions.quote: Tertiary activities are basically concerned with the distribution of primary and secondary products through a system of transport and trade. (e.g.) Banking, Trade and Communications.

en.q: Banking, trade and communications are examples of ______ activities.
en.explanation: Tertiary activities distribute primary and secondary products.

ta.q: வங்கி, வணிகம், தகவல் தொடர்பு ஆகியவை ______ செயல்பாடுகளுக்கு எடுத்துக்காட்டுகள்.

questions.quote: The easiest way to conserve resources is to follow the '3R's: Reduce, Reuse and Recycle.

en.q: The three Rs of conservation of resources are ______.
en.explanation: It is the easiest way to conserve resources.

questions.quote: Resource planning is a technique or skill of proper utilization of resources. Resource planning is necessary because resources are limited and unevenly distributed over the different parts of the World.

en.q: Resource planning is a technique or skill of ______.
en.explanation: It is necessary because resources are limited and unevenly distributed.

ta.explanation: வளங்கள் குறைவு, சீரற்ற பரவல் உடையவை என்பதால் அது தேவை.
